# Realign the code with its documented specification

The repository at `/app` is `dpath`, filesystem-like path traversal, globbing, mutation, and merging for nested Python objects. Its intended behaviour is defined by the
project's own **documentation** — README.rst and the docstrings of low-level helpers in dpath/segments.py and dpath/__init__.py. The code currently **runs fine**, but its behaviour
has **drifted from that documented specification**: in one or more places the code does something
subtly different from what its documentation says — a plausible-looking default or condition that is
nonetheless wrong per the docs.

## Your job
Study the documented behaviour (README.rst and the docstrings of low-level helpers in dpath/segments.py and dpath/__init__.py) and compare it against the implementation. Find
wherever the code disagrees with its own documentation and fix it so the behaviour matches the docs
again. Edit only the implementation under `/app/dpath/` — keep the public API, signatures, and
file layout unchanged; add no files.

## How you are graded (binary, all-or-nothing)
Your code is checked against the documented behaviour on many held-out inputs (path normalization and low-level segment/glob helper calls, plus public search/get/new regression calls). You
score **1.0 only if the behaviour matches the specification everywhere it is checked**, otherwise
0.0. The checks are not in this checkout — locate the divergence by reasoning about the docs vs the
code, not
